Yoga isn't about touching your toes.
*It's about coming home to yourself.*

about_alt: A group of people practising yoga outdoors in a leafy park at golden hour
about_text:
I've been practising yoga for over 16 years, and following my heart led me to become a certified Sivananda Hatha Yoga Teacher (Siromani).

This summer, I started teaching a small yoga class in the park. What began as a simple idea grew into a lovely group of 8–10 wonderful souls. Watching our friendly community grow week by week has been an absolute joy.

As the seasons change, we're bringing our practice indoors to a cosy studio space. Whether you've joined me before or are stepping onto a yoga mat for the very first time, there's a place for you here.
practice_text: Each 75-minute class follows the balanced principles of classical Sivananda Hatha Yoga, with room to listen to your own body and find your own pace.

Wear comfortable clothes that let you move. Please ask when booking whether mats and any other equipment are provided, or bring your own mat if you have one.

journal_alt: A ginger cat stretching on a wooden floor, front paws reaching far forward and hips raised
journal_title: Cat pose (Marjaryasana): what our feline friends can teach us
journal_text:
Ever watched a cat wake from a nap? Before doing anything else, it stretches — front paws reaching long, hips lifted, spine lengthening, with no rush at all. Yoga borrowed the idea long ago: *Marjaryasana*, or Cat Pose, takes its name from the Sanskrit word for cat.

On hands and knees you round the spine towards the ceiling, then lift the chest into Cow Pose (*Bitilasana*) as you breathe in. Together they make a gentle warm-up for the back and a lovely way to link movement with breath. The stretch our model is enjoying above is closer to Downward-Facing Dog — another pose inspired by animals.

journal_steps.text: Come onto hands and knees, wrists under shoulders, knees under hips.
Breathe out: round your back, let the head hang softly.
Breathe in: lift the chest and tailbone, letting the belly soften.
Repeat for 5–8 slow breaths. Move gently and stop if anything hurts.
